paper.title: Self-organized criticality in a continuous, nonconservative cellular automaton modeling earthquakes

headline: OFC 1992 earthquakes (driven-threshold CA / SOC): 3/3 locked clauses REPRO; alpha=0.2 size range 2.10 decades, max 125 (>=100x median); mean event size 1.73 (alpha=0.2) > 1.08 (alpha=0.1); distribution stationary + init-independent (TV <= 0.027)

verdicts.gate: P1 heavy-tailed event sizes (alpha=0.2): >=2 decades AND max >= 100x median nonzero
P2 more conservative alpha gives a heavier tail: mean event size at alpha=0.2 > at alpha=0.1
P3 stationary + init-independent critical state: two-halves AND two-seed distributions match

extra.scope: faithful reproduction of a published synthetic SOC model; no real-world data; the contribution is whether the harness + discipline reproduce self-organized criticality (a heavy-tailed, alpha-dependent, stationary + init-independent avalanche-size distribution) and would catch an artifact

citations: Olami, Z., Feder, H.J.S. & Christensen, K. (1992). Self-organized criticality in a continuous, nonconservative cellular automaton modeling earthquakes. Phys. Rev. Lett. 68(8):1244-1247. doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.68.1244.

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful single-implementation reproduction graded against the avalanche (event-size) distribution: decades spanned, max/median ratio, alpha dependence, and stationarity + init-independence
